features.title: Barcode scanning
features.benefit: Find the right item with a scan.
features.problem: A long line is the wrong time to type every product name.
features.workflow: Scan a recorded barcode, check the matching item and size, then add it to the basket.
features.example: A customer arrives with six perennial tags. Staff check each scanned match before taking payment.
features.fit: Scanner compatibility and readable labels need a check with your equipment.

features.title: Plant search
features.benefit: Find the plant the customer means.
features.problem: Customers and staff often know the same plant by different names.
features.workflow: Search recorded common names, botanical names and aliases, then confirm the variant.
features.example: A customer asks for a hydrangea while the tag uses its botanical name. Both can lead staff to the recorded plant.
features.fit: Search results depend on the names and aliases in your catalogue.

features.title: Missing-tag lookup
features.benefit: Keep a missing tag from stopping the sale.
features.problem: A plant reaches the counter without a usable label.
features.workflow: Use the photo, name or price lookup to narrow the choices and confirm the pot size.
features.example: A customer brings an untagged hosta. The cashier compares the catalogue picture and size before adding it.
features.fit: Photos help identify candidates; staff still confirm the actual product and price.

features.title: Visual product browsing
features.benefit: Give seasonal staff something they can recognize.
features.problem: A new cashier may recognize the plant before they remember its name.
features.workflow: Browse recorded product photos and choose the correct selling option.
features.example: A seasonal hire uses the product image to distinguish a planter from a hanging basket.
features.fit: Products need suitable photos. Images are a reference, not a guarantee of the specimen's appearance.

features.title: Basket editing
features.benefit: Fix the basket before the payment starts.
features.problem: Customers change quantities or decide against an item at the counter.
features.workflow: Review quantities, remove unwanted items and check the recalculated total.
features.example: A customer chooses two bags of soil instead of three. Staff correct the basket before tendering.
features.fit: Once payment is underway, follow the payment cancellation or recovery workflow before changing the basket.

features.title: Pack and flat selling
features.benefit: Sell the way your plants are packaged.
features.problem: Eaches, packs and flats can make quantities confusing.
features.workflow: Select a configured selling unit and let the recorded conversion determine the stock quantity.
features.example: A shopper buys a flat rather than individual plants. The selected selling unit keeps the sale tied to its conversion.
features.fit: Configure pack ratios and prices correctly before use.

features.title: Measured product sales
features.benefit: Handle the quantities your customers actually buy.
features.problem: Bulk products do not always sell in whole pieces.
features.workflow: Use a configured measured unit and record the exact quantity for the sale.
features.example: A customer buys a measured amount of bulk material instead of a whole packaged item.
features.fit: Supported units require configuration; connected scales and local measurement requirements need separate verification.

features.title: Price overrides
features.benefit: Handle a fair exception with a clear reason.
features.problem: An occasional damaged pot or agreed price needs a controlled adjustment.
features.workflow: Request the price change, record the reason and follow the configured approval policy.
features.example: A manager authorizes a reduced price for a scratched planter while keeping the reason with the transaction.
features.fit: Your store sets the approval policy. Staff access does not imply unrestricted discount authority.

features.title: Cashier handover
features.benefit: Hand the till over with confidence.
features.problem: Shared registers can blur who handled the next sale.
features.workflow: Finish or void the current basket, choose Switch cashier and let the next staff member sign in.
features.example: The morning cashier hands over after lunch without leaving the next sale under their name.
features.fit: New cashier sign-in needs connectivity; this is not an offline sign-in promise.

features.title: Cashier practice
features.benefit: Give new staff a place to get comfortable.
features.problem: The first spring Saturday is a difficult time to learn checkout.
features.workflow: Rehearse finding products, correcting baskets, taking payment and closing with demonstration data.
features.example: A new seasonal employee practises a return before serving their first customer.
features.fit: Practice uses demonstration data. Real staff acceptance and hardware rehearsal remain part of onboarding.

features.title: Cash checkout
features.benefit: Make cash and change easier to follow.
features.problem: Mental arithmetic at a busy counter creates unnecessary pressure.
features.workflow: Enter the cash received, review the displayed change and finish the recorded sale.
features.example: A customer pays with a larger note. The cashier follows the displayed change amount and supplies the receipt.
features.fit: Cash rounding follows the configured jurisdiction. Physical drawer compatibility needs verification.

features.title: Integrated card payments
features.benefit: Remove the extra amount-entry step.
features.problem: Typing the till total into a separate terminal creates a chance for rekeying errors.
features.workflow: The integrated payment flow sends the amount to the configured reader and waits for a confirmed result.
features.example: A busy cashier can follow one payment flow rather than manually enter a second total on another device.
features.fit: Reader, merchant account, country and provider setup require verification. Hardware and live-store acceptance are separate from the software build.

features.title: Split payments
features.benefit: Let a basket use more than one payment method.
features.problem: A customer may want to use a balance and pay the rest another way.
features.workflow: Record the supported tenders against the same sale and review the amount still outstanding.
features.example: A shopper uses an eligible gift-card balance and pays the remainder with another supported tender.
features.fit: Available combinations depend on configuration and online balance checks. Card processing requires verified setup.

features.title: Payment recovery
features.benefit: Know what to do when the answer is unclear.
features.problem: A lost connection can leave staff unsure whether a payment completed.
features.workflow: Review the retained attempt and reconcile its provider status before deciding the next action.
features.example: The screen reloads during a card payment. Staff check the original outcome before starting another attempt.
features.fit: An uncertain payment needs reconciliation; never assume failure and charge again.

features.title: Card payment cancellation
features.benefit: Handle a changed mind during payment.
features.problem: A customer may remove an item after a payment attempt has started.
features.workflow: Use the supported cancel or reversal path and resolve the payment before rebuilding the basket.
features.example: A shopper changes their mind during a split payment. Staff resolve the captured or uncaptured portion first.
features.fit: Cancellation and reversal depend on the provider's actual payment state and configured integration.

features.title: Gift-card balances
features.benefit: Keep gift value separate and traceable.
features.problem: Gift cards need a balance history that survives partial use.
features.workflow: Review issuance, redemption and reversal records in the gift-card ledger.
features.example: A shopper spends part of a gift card now and returns later for the remaining value.
features.fit: Balance use requires the complete card code and authorized online checks. Issuance needs a valid funding workflow.

features.title: Store credit
features.benefit: Keep a return credit connected to its history.
features.problem: Paper credit notes are easy to lose and difficult to reconcile.
features.workflow: Issue authorized credit, review its balance and retain the related return and redemption records.
features.example: A customer accepts store credit for an eligible return and later uses part of it.
features.fit: Store credit and gift cards are separate liabilities. Your return policy controls eligibility.

features.title: Original-tender returns
features.benefit: Return value through the right route.
features.problem: Refunding every return as cash can distort balances and leave liabilities incorrect.
features.workflow: Find the original sale, select the return quantity and follow its supported original-tender refund path.
features.example: An item bought using store credit is returned with the credit ledger corrected as part of the workflow.
features.fit: Provider refunds and account permissions must be configured. Mixed tenders retain their original allocations.

features.title: Refund progress
features.benefit: Keep an unresolved refund visible.
features.problem: Customers and staff need clarity when a refund is pending or fails.
features.workflow: Review the recorded refund state and follow up on unresolved outcomes.
features.example: A refund needs provider confirmation. The manager can distinguish the pending record from a completed refund.
features.fit: A recorded request does not mean the bank has completed a refund; provider timing applies.

features.title: Payment history
features.benefit: Keep the payment trail close to the sale.
features.problem: A question at closing should not require reconstructing the day from memory.
features.workflow: Review the original payment attempts, recorded outcomes and related corrections.
features.example: A manager investigates a customer's payment question using the retained transaction history.
features.fit: Recorded evidence supports review. Reconcile provider settlements separately before treating them as deposited funds.

features.title: Common and botanical names
features.benefit: Speak both gardener and grower.
features.problem: Plant knowledge varies across your customers, staff and suppliers.
features.workflow: Keep common and botanical names on the same plant identity.
features.example: The grower's list uses a botanical name while the shopper uses a common name. Staff can check both.
features.fit: Accurate identity still needs catalogue review; names alone do not establish a verified plant match.

features.title: Product variants
features.benefit: Give every pot size its own place.
features.problem: A one-gallon and a five-gallon plant should not share an ambiguous selling record.
features.workflow: Create sellable variants with the appropriate pot, grade or colour and pricing.
features.example: The same shrub is available in two sizes. Staff choose the correct variant at the counter.
features.fit: Variants need their own accurate identifiers and selling configuration.

features.title: Product photographs
features.benefit: Help staff recognize what they are selling.
features.problem: A name-only list makes unfamiliar plants and giftware harder to find.
features.workflow: Review the main photo in the catalogue and replace it through the product-photo workflow.
features.example: A manager updates a planter's main image so cashiers can recognize it more easily.
features.fit: Use images you have rights to publish. Catalogue pictures may differ from current living specimens.

features.title: Alternate barcodes
features.benefit: Recognize more than one label for the same item.
features.problem: Supplier labels and in-store labels may use different codes.
features.workflow: Record the permitted barcode aliases against the intended sellable variant.
features.example: Two shipments use different UPCs for the same pot size. Staff maintain the aliases in one product record.
features.fit: Duplicate identifiers need review; the same code must not ambiguously identify two variants.

features.title: Supplier product codes
features.benefit: Keep supplier references near the product.
features.problem: Reordering becomes slower when staff cannot connect a supplier code to the item.
features.workflow: Retain vendor SKUs and supplier mappings alongside product variants.
features.example: A grower invoice uses a vendor code that differs from the store's SKU. The mapping keeps the relationship visible.
features.fit: Supplier mappings need verification, especially when pack sizes or item specifications change.

features.title: Product aliases
features.benefit: Find products using the words your team uses.
features.problem: Abbreviations and familiar nicknames do not always match official names.
features.workflow: Add useful search aliases to the recorded plant identity.
features.example: Staff search a commonly used nickname and confirm the correct named plant in the result.
features.fit: Aliases improve lookup; staff still verify size and identity before selling.

features.title: Product selling units
features.benefit: Keep eaches, weights and volumes understandable.
features.problem: Different departments sell in different units.
features.workflow: Configure the stock unit, selling units and conversion ratios for a variant.
features.example: Plants sell by each while a bulk material uses a measured unit. Both retain their configured quantity relationship.
features.fit: Unit configuration must match store practice; physical weighing devices require their own compatibility review.

features.title: Catalogue price editing
features.benefit: Keep everyday price changes manageable.
features.problem: A price correction should not require hunting through unrelated screens.
features.workflow: Open the product variant, review the price and save the intended change with the existing controls.
features.example: A manager corrects the regular selling price for a new pot size before it reaches the counter.
features.fit: Confirm tax treatment and selling units separately. A base-price edit does not automatically change every channel.

features.title: Seasonal pricing
features.benefit: Plan price changes around your season.
features.problem: Spring promotions and end-of-season markdowns need clear timing.
features.workflow: Use the supported seasonal-price workflow and review the affected variants and dates.
features.example: A manager prepares a price period for a seasonal selection instead of relying on a note at each till.
features.fit: Review overlapping prices, dates and store policy before activation; no sales uplift is guaranteed.

features.title: Product setup review
features.benefit: Catch catalogue problems before they reach checkout.
features.problem: An import with a wrong size or price can create many small counter problems.
features.workflow: Preview the proposed product records, resolve validation issues and apply the reviewed source.
features.example: Before switching systems, the owner checks names and selling prices rather than accepting an unchecked file.
features.fit: Product setup is separate from opening stock, historical sales and customer balances.

features.title: Stock lookup
features.benefit: Give staff a stock figure they can explain.
features.problem: A number is useful only when staff know what it represents.
features.workflow: Review recorded store stock and its available context while serving the customer.
features.example: A cashier checks the recorded quantity before asking a colleague to look in the greenhouse.
features.fit: Recorded stock is not a physical count or an unconditional promise of availability; freshness and reservations matter.

features.title: Stock areas
features.benefit: Keep track of where stock belongs.
features.problem: The greenhouse, yard and back room are different places to look.
features.workflow: Organize stock using configured store areas and location-aware records.
features.example: A team member can distinguish a greenhouse quantity from stock recorded in another area.
features.fit: Area setup and accurate movement recording are needed; this is not automatic physical tracking.

features.title: Plant-loss recording
features.benefit: See where living stock is being lost.
features.problem: Dead or damaged plants can disappear from stock without a useful explanation.
features.workflow: Record the quantity, condition and garden-specific loss reason with its evidence.
features.example: The team records a tray lost to damage so the owner can review the reason later.
features.fit: Known loss stays separate from unexplained count variance. Cost figures may be estimates.

features.title: Blind inventory counts
features.benefit: Get a count based on what staff see.
features.problem: Showing an expected number first can bias a count.
features.workflow: Record a blind first count before reviewing the expected quantity and differences.
features.example: A staff member counts a bench without being prompted to match the system quantity.
features.fit: Use the supported online workflow; disconnected handheld counting is not implied.

features.title: Variance recounts
features.benefit: Give a surprising difference a second look.
features.problem: A large mismatch may be a counting mistake rather than actual stock loss.
features.workflow: Retain the original count and require a recount when the configured variance threshold applies.
features.example: A large shrub discrepancy prompts a second count before the manager posts an adjustment.
features.fit: Thresholds and approvals need configuration. A recount adds evidence rather than replacing the first count.

features.title: Count adjustments
features.benefit: Correct stock with a reason you can revisit.
features.problem: Directly replacing a quantity makes it hard to explain what changed.
features.workflow: Approve the reviewed variance and post a linked stock adjustment.
features.example: After a recount, the manager approves the documented difference and can trace the resulting movement.
features.fit: Count approval and posting are distinct steps. Review ongoing movements during trading.

features.title: Damaged stock
features.benefit: Keep questionable plants out of the ready-to-sell pile.
features.problem: A damaged delivery should not look like healthy sellable stock.
features.workflow: Record damaged or quarantined quantities in the appropriate condition bucket.
features.example: A cracked pot or unhealthy tray is recorded separately while the team decides what to do.
features.fit: Physical separation remains a staff job. Moving stock back to sellable condition needs an authorized decision.

features.title: Stock movement history
features.benefit: Understand why the quantity changed.
features.problem: A stock total alone does not explain receipts, losses or corrections.
features.workflow: Review the recorded movements behind a stock position.
features.example: An owner investigates a discrepancy by checking receiving, loss and adjustment records.
features.fit: Movement history reflects recorded operations; missing physical handling must still be investigated.

features.title: Inter-store transfers
features.benefit: Move stock without losing sight of it.
features.problem: Stock between two stores should not vanish from both records.
features.workflow: Request, approve, ship and receive a transfer with source and destination evidence.
features.example: One location sends shrubs to another and records a partial receipt when the second truck arrives.
features.fit: Each store and register must be correctly configured. A transfer is not a retail sale.

features.title: In-transit stock
features.benefit: See what is still on the way.
features.problem: Shipped stock is not yet ready to sell at the receiving store.
features.workflow: Review the quantities shipped, received and still in transit on a transfer.
features.example: The owner can distinguish plants on the truck from plants confirmed at the destination.
features.fit: Transit status depends on staff posting shipment and receipt events accurately.

features.title: Saved suppliers
features.benefit: Stop retyping the same supplier details.
features.problem: Repeat orders should start with the information the store already has.
features.workflow: Choose a recorded supplier and review its saved contact and purchasing details.
features.example: The buyer starts another grower order using an existing supplier record.
features.fit: Saved details need periodic review. The system does not invent missing supplier contacts.

features.title: Purchase orders
features.benefit: Give buying decisions a clear record.
features.problem: Orders spread across notes and emails are harder to track.
features.workflow: Create a supplier purchase order with its lines, units and expected costs.
features.example: A buyer builds a spring plant order the manager can review before approval.
features.fit: An internal order record does not automatically email or place an order with a supplier.

features.title: Purchase approvals
features.benefit: Keep purchasing authority clear.
features.problem: A draft order should not silently become an approved commitment.
features.workflow: Submit the order for review and approve it through the authorized workflow.
features.example: A seasonal buyer prepares the order while the owner retains approval authority.
features.fit: Configure staff access and purchasing policy. Supplier acceptance remains a separate business step.

features.title: Partial receiving
features.benefit: Record the delivery you actually got.
features.problem: A supplier may deliver one order over more than one truck.
features.workflow: Receive the quantities delivered while retaining the open order balance.
features.example: Half the ordered perennials arrive today. Staff record this delivery without marking the remainder received.
features.fit: Only confirmed receipt quantities should affect stock. Review exceptions before posting.

features.title: Receiving exceptions
features.benefit: Explain short, extra or substituted items.
features.problem: Deliveries rarely match every order line perfectly.
features.workflow: Record overages, shortages and substitutions with the required reason.
features.example: A grower substitutes a pot size. Staff document the exception before confirming the received stock.
features.fit: Staff must verify product identity, units and the commercial arrangement with the supplier.

features.title: Freight and landed costs
features.benefit: See more of the cost behind the purchase.
features.problem: The supplier's item price may not include freight or duty.
features.workflow: Allocate recorded landed-cost components across the received goods using the supported workflow.
features.example: A delivery charge is allocated across the receipt so the owner can review its cost impact.
features.fit: Recorded allocations depend on accurate inputs and are not a substitute for accounting advice or a verified inventory valuation.

features.title: Supplier pack conversions
features.benefit: Turn supplier packs into understandable stock.
features.problem: The grower sells by tray while the store sells by plant.
features.workflow: Map supplier packs to product variants and record the exact conversion ratio.
features.example: Receiving ten trays produces the configured plant quantity rather than ten individual plants.
features.fit: Review ratios when a supplier changes its pack size. Incorrect mappings cause incorrect quantities.

features.title: Low-stock reordering
features.benefit: Turn a stock alert into the next useful step.
features.problem: An alert is less helpful when it leaves the owner to start from a blank screen.
features.workflow: Open the linked New order workflow and review saved supplier and receipt-based suggestions.
features.example: A low-stock email points the buyer toward a new order with relevant history available.
features.fit: Email delivery must be configured. Suggestions are reviewed defaults, not automatic purchasing or demand forecasting.

features.title: Repeat supplier orders
features.benefit: Make repeat buying less repetitive.
features.problem: A buyer should not have to reconstruct the last sensible order every time.
features.workflow: Review historical supplier, pack and cost defaults before preparing the next order.
features.example: The next soil order starts with the recorded pack details from a prior receipt.
features.fit: Defaults apply only where the source and pack remain eligible. Historical costs are not current supplier quotes.

features.title: Photo-assisted receiving
features.benefit: Start the paperwork from the delivery document.
features.problem: Entering a packing slip manually can slow the receiving team.
features.workflow: Open an approved purchase order, upload the packing slip, then check suggested matches and quantities before confirming the receipt.
features.example: Staff photograph a packing slip, then compare the suggested lines with the actual trays on the truck.
features.fit: Requires an approved purchase order, manager access and configured document assistance. Suggestions can be wrong; staff review the goods before confirming any stock change.

features.title: Customer lookup
features.benefit: Find the person without starting another record.
features.problem: Repeat customers should not accumulate a new profile on every visit.
features.workflow: Search recorded name, phone or email and confirm the intended customer.
features.example: A regular shopper gives a phone number so staff can find the existing profile.
features.fit: Staff must check the match. Ordinary anonymous sales do not require a customer record.

features.title: Customer duplicate review
features.benefit: Bring confirmed duplicates together carefully.
features.problem: Duplicate profiles split the customer's story and create extra work.
features.workflow: Review the candidates and merge an eligible confirmed duplicate while retaining history.
features.example: A manager resolves two records for the same shopper after checking the details.
features.fit: Conflicting identities or trade accounts can block a merge. Similar names alone are insufficient evidence.

features.title: Trade account terms
features.benefit: Serve landscapers with the right arrangement.
features.problem: A contractor's purchasing needs differ from a walk-in shopper's.
features.workflow: Record the trade account's terms, price-tier reference and purchase-order requirements.
features.example: A landscaping company has a documented account arrangement staff can check before a charge sale.
features.fit: Terms need owner approval. An account record alone does not grant every buyer charging authority.

features.title: Authorized trade buyers
features.benefit: Know who can buy for an account.
features.problem: Someone naming a landscaping company may not be authorized to charge it.
features.workflow: Record eligible buyers and their effective dates against the trade account.
features.example: The crew leader is permitted to charge materials while an expired buyer is no longer eligible.
features.fit: Charging authority is scoped and time-bound. It does not provide account administration access.

features.title: Customer purchase-order references
features.benefit: Keep a contractor's job paperwork together.
features.problem: An invoice without the customer's PO can create a payment delay.
features.workflow: Capture required customer PO and job context with the sale and account workflow.
features.example: The landscaper supplies a project PO before the charge invoice is posted.
features.fit: PO requirements depend on account configuration. Staff must verify the customer's actual reference.

features.title: Charge accounts
features.benefit: Give approved trade sales a proper ledger.
features.problem: Pay-later sales need more than a note saying who owes what.
features.workflow: Post eligible charge invoices to an active account with buyer, sale and tax context.
features.example: A verified buyer purchases materials on an approved company account.
features.fit: Online authorization, account status, credit policy and required PO details apply.

features.title: Credit-limit controls
features.benefit: Keep account exposure visible at checkout.
features.problem: A busy cashier should not have to guess whether a charge is within terms.
features.workflow: Use the account's server-checked eligibility and limit decision for the charge workflow.
features.example: A proposed trade purchase exceeds the account's available limit and requires resolution.
features.fit: Do not treat an old cached balance as available credit. Overrides follow configured authority.

features.title: Account statements
features.benefit: Make the account conversation easier.
features.problem: Customers need an understandable view of invoices and what is still due.
features.workflow: Review the account ledger and prepare the supported statement view.
features.example: A contractor asks which invoices remain unpaid. Staff use the recorded account history.
features.fit: Confirm payment allocations and account details before sharing. A statement is not automatic collection activity.

features.title: Receivable payments
features.benefit: Record a payment without counting the sale twice.
features.problem: Settling an old invoice is different from making a new retail sale.
features.workflow: Apply the recorded payment to the eligible account balance and retain its allocation.
features.example: A landscaping company pays an outstanding invoice without creating new product revenue.
features.fit: Use the supported account-payment process. Reconcile payment-provider settlements separately.

features.title: Tax-exemption evidence
features.benefit: Keep the evidence behind an exemption close.
features.problem: A blanket tax-exempt checkbox can overlook dates and eligible uses.
features.workflow: Review certificate evidence against jurisdiction, dates, product category and intended use.
features.example: A trade buyer's certificate is checked for the actual purchase rather than assumed valid forever.
features.fit: The owner must confirm local tax policy and evidence. Software does not determine legal eligibility on its own.

features.title: Special orders
features.benefit: Give a customer request a proper home.
features.problem: A plant ordered for one customer can get lost among ordinary stock tasks.
features.workflow: Create a customer-linked special order with lines and agreed terms.
features.example: A customer requests a particular specimen shrub and staff can find the order later.
features.fit: Availability, supplier commitment and final fulfilment need confirmation; a record does not guarantee supply.

features.title: Customer deposits
features.benefit: Keep money held for an order understandable.
features.problem: A deposit is not the same as a completed product sale.
features.workflow: Record order payments separately and apply eligible deposits through fulfilment.
features.example: A customer leaves a deposit for a special-order tree before it arrives.
features.fit: Cancellation, forfeiture and refund terms need store approval. Deposits remain separate from ordinary sale revenue until applied.

features.title: Partial fulfilment
features.benefit: Let customers collect what has arrived.
features.problem: Waiting for one missing item should not make the rest of an order confusing.
features.workflow: Record the fulfilled quantities and retain the outstanding order lines.
features.example: Two of three ordered shrubs arrive. Staff fulfil the two while keeping the third open.
features.fit: Review deposit application and remaining balances during each fulfilment.

features.title: Layaway records
features.benefit: Keep staged payments and pickup terms together.
features.problem: A held purchase needs clear payment and collection records.
features.workflow: Use the supported deferred-order workflow to retain terms and payments.
features.example: A customer arranges staged payments for an eligible purchase and the team reviews its progress.
features.fit: Store policy determines whether layaway is offered. Confirm reservation and cancellation terms explicitly.

features.title: Rain checks
features.benefit: Remember a promise to revisit availability.
features.problem: An out-of-stock request deserves a record without pretending stock exists.
features.workflow: Create a rain-check record with the customer and agreed terms.
features.example: A customer asks about a sold-out plant. Staff retain the request for follow-up review.
features.fit: A rain check does not reserve stock or promise that the supplier will have the item.

features.title: Order cancellations
features.benefit: Resolve the order and its money together.
features.problem: Deleting a cancelled order would erase the agreement and payment trail.
features.workflow: Use the cancellation workflow and review associated deposits, allocations and refunds.
features.example: A customer cancels a special order; staff retain the decision and handle the eligible financial correction.
features.fit: Policy, authorization and provider outcomes govern refunds. A cancellation record alone does not prove money was returned.

features.title: Pickup planning
features.benefit: Give collection day a workable plan.
features.problem: A list of names is not enough when many customers arrive together.
features.workflow: Build the supported pickup batches and review assigned orders and capacity.
features.example: A spring presale is organized into manageable pickup groups for the team.
features.fit: Staff still prepare goods, confirm readiness and carry out the physical handover.

features.title: Delivery planning
features.benefit: Keep delivery arrangements visible to the team.
features.problem: Addresses and agreed delivery details can get scattered across notes.
features.workflow: Review orders and their recorded delivery arrangements in the owner workspace.
features.example: A manager checks the day's delivery work and the details that need confirmation.
features.fit: This is planning support. Route optimization, carrier booking and automatic shipping are not implied.

features.title: Presale campaigns
features.benefit: Organize demand before the selling window closes.
features.problem: Seasonal presales need clear offers, quantities and order tracking.
features.workflow: Configure the campaign selling window, offers and allocation caps and review orders.
features.example: The store prepares a limited seasonal presale and tracks its recorded allocations.
features.fit: Connected channel setup and verified allocation rules are required before accepting live orders.

features.title: Fundraiser reconciliation
features.benefit: See the orders behind the fundraiser total.
features.problem: Fundraisers can mix online and in-store orders, refunds and commissions.
features.workflow: Review campaign orders, collections, refunds and provisional attribution together.
features.example: A school fundraiser coordinator's total can be reviewed against the underlying recorded orders.
features.fit: Website connection and shared identity require setup. Provisional commission is subject to final reconciliation.

features.title: Staff PIN sign-in
features.benefit: Make the active cashier clear.
features.problem: A shared counter should still record who performed the work.
features.workflow: Choose the staff identity and sign in through the bound register's PIN workflow.
features.example: A new shift starts with the correct staff member identified on the register.
features.fit: Device binding and permissions must be set up. PIN handling does not replace your staff access policy.

features.title: Store-scoped roles
features.benefit: Give people the access their work needs.
features.problem: A cashier should not automatically get every owner control.
features.workflow: Grant cashier, supervisor, manager or owner roles within the intended store scope.
features.example: A supervisor can handle the approved work at one location without managing the whole business.
features.fit: Owners must review grants and revoke access when responsibilities change.

features.title: Manager approvals
features.benefit: Make sensitive decisions visible.
features.problem: Refunds and overrides need a clear point of accountability.
features.workflow: Apply configured thresholds and retain the actor, approver and reason.
features.example: An above-threshold refund reaches an authorized manager instead of relying on an informal nod.
features.fit: Approval availability depends on policy and cached authorization where offline support applies.

features.title: Action audit trail
features.benefit: Answer who changed what and why.
features.problem: The owner cannot be standing beside every counter all day.
features.workflow: Review retained action, staff, approver, device, time and before-and-after evidence.
features.example: A manager investigates a price exception and can see who approved it and the recorded reason.
features.fit: The audit reflects recorded actions and permissions; it does not monitor physical activity.

features.title: Opening floats
features.benefit: Start the drawer from an agreed amount.
features.problem: A confusing starting cash figure makes the end of the day harder.
features.workflow: Open the register session and record the counted opening float.
features.example: The morning cashier counts the float before serving the first shopper.
features.fit: A staff member must physically count cash. A software record does not verify the contents of a drawer.

features.title: Paid in and paid out
features.benefit: Explain cash that moves outside a sale.
features.problem: Petty-cash movements can look like unexplained drawer differences.
features.workflow: Record the supported paid-in or paid-out movement with its reason and authority.
features.example: A permitted cash movement is documented so the closer can explain it later.
features.fit: Follow your store's cash-handling rules and approval thresholds.

features.title: Register assignments
features.benefit: Keep the register tied to the right store.
features.problem: A device label alone is not a reliable store identity.
features.workflow: Bind the register to its intended store and retain that context with sessions and sales.
features.example: A second location opens its own register without mixing its session context with the first store.
features.fit: Reassigning a register needs controlled setup and review of outstanding local work.

features.title: Multi-store configuration
features.benefit: Give each location its own operating context.
features.problem: Locations may differ in timezone, policy or registration details.
features.workflow: Configure the business entity, reporting currency, stores and effective policies.
features.example: The owner reviews each store in the right context while retaining a business-wide view.
features.fit: Confirm entity, currency and tax configuration before trading. Consolidation does not imply currency conversion.

features.title: Tablet-friendly workspaces
features.benefit: Bring store work closer to where it happens.
features.problem: Managers are not always sitting at a desk when work arrives.
features.workflow: Use the responsive manager workspace to review and complete supported tasks.
features.example: A manager reviews catalogue details from a tablet while working near the receiving area.
features.fit: Browser, network and peripherals need checks on the actual device. Responsive layout is not a hardware certification.

features.title: Guided store setup
features.benefit: See what needs attention before opening.
features.problem: Missing configuration is easier to resolve before customers are waiting.
features.workflow: Follow setup checks for business details, staff, catalogue, register and payment readiness.
features.example: An owner reviews outstanding setup items with the team before planning the cutover.
features.fit: Go-live requires confirmed merchant, device, policy and staff acceptance; a completed form alone is insufficient.

features.title: Sales reporting
features.benefit: Turn recorded sales into a clearer view.
features.problem: Owners need more than a total to understand the working day.
features.workflow: Review the supported store and period reports with their coverage and source context.
features.example: An owner reviews the day's recorded activity before discussing tomorrow's priorities.
features.fit: Reports depend on synchronized and projected records. Incomplete data must not be interpreted as zero activity.

features.title: Cash-count comparison
features.benefit: See the difference while the day is fresh.
features.problem: A drawer mismatch is harder to understand days later.
features.workflow: Enter the actual cash count and compare it with the session's recorded expectation.
features.example: The closer spots a difference and reviews cash movements before signing off.
features.fit: The expected figure depends on recorded opening, sales, refunds and cash movements.

features.title: End-of-day close
features.benefit: Give closing a clear finish line.
features.problem: Closing needs a repeatable routine even after a long day.
features.workflow: Resolve outstanding payment work, count cash, review differences and close the session.
features.example: The team follows one close sequence rather than leaving unresolved items for the next shift.
features.fit: Uncertain payments and incomplete records need resolution; physical count and owner policy still apply.

features.title: Z reports
features.benefit: Retain a useful record of the closed session.
features.problem: The closing conversation should have a record to return to.
features.workflow: Review the supported Z-report output for the completed register session.
features.example: The owner checks the retained close summary when following up on a cash difference.
features.fit: A close report summarizes recorded session activity. Bank settlement and accounting review remain separate.

features.title: Refunds at daily close
features.benefit: Keep refunds in the session that handled them.
features.problem: A return today for an older sale should not quietly rewrite today's cash story.
features.workflow: Retain the original sale linkage while attributing the refund to its actual session.
features.example: A customer returns yesterday's purchase today. The return history and today's drawer impact remain connected.
features.fit: Review original tender and provider refund state alongside session totals.

features.title: Tender reconciliation
features.benefit: Compare how value was collected.
features.problem: Cash, cards and account payments need their own explanations.
features.workflow: Review the recorded tender breakdown against the underlying sales and corrections.
features.example: At closing, the manager compares cash movements and card records rather than relying on one blended total.
features.fit: Provider fees, payout timing and external settlement require separate reconciliation.

features.title: Tax reporting
features.benefit: Keep collected tax tied to its records.
features.problem: Owners need to understand which transactions produced a tax amount.
features.workflow: Review the supported tax breakdowns and retained sale tax context.
features.example: The owner prepares recorded tax information for the person reviewing the business accounts.
features.fit: Jurisdiction setup and professional review are required. Reports do not constitute tax filing or legal advice.

features.title: Owner exception review
features.benefit: See what needs a closer look.
features.problem: A neat dashboard can hide work still waiting for reconciliation.
features.workflow: Review recorded close mismatches, payment findings and incomplete sources as exceptions.
features.example: An owner starts with the items needing review before treating the day as fully reconciled.
features.fit: An exception is a review signal, not proof of a failed charge. Missing data is shown as unavailable.

features.title: Business data exports
features.benefit: Keep access to your business records.
features.problem: Owners should be able to review information outside the application when needed.
features.workflow: Prepare the supported store-scoped CSV or JSON archive through the authorized export process.
features.example: An owner prepares an archive for review while retaining the source context.
features.fit: Export scope, size and included records need review. An export is not a tested disaster-recovery restore.

features.title: QuickBooks accounting preparation
features.benefit: Make the accounting handoff easier to review.
features.problem: Sales, deposits, gift value and account settlements should not all be treated as the same revenue.
features.workflow: Review the daily accounting source and supported journal preparation before any posting.
features.example: The owner and bookkeeper inspect the sales, tax, tender and liability breakdown together.
features.fit: QuickBooks connection, approved company setup, accountant review and provider acceptance are required. Automatic live posting is not promised.

features.title: Plant care guidance
features.benefit: Help the customer care for what they bought.
features.problem: A good plant sale still needs useful light, water and soil advice.
features.workflow: Review and publish available source-backed care against the confirmed product identity.
features.example: A staff member checks the approved care for the plant rather than inventing a watering interval from its name.
features.fit: Care coverage varies. Missing advice stays missing until reviewed; AI-generated care for every product is not included.

features.title: Branded email receipts
features.benefit: Send something useful after the visit.
features.problem: A receipt should be understandable and easy for the customer to keep.
features.workflow: Capture the receipt request and send the recorded branded receipt through the configured delivery workflow.
features.example: A shopper requests an email copy so they can find the purchase later.
features.fit: Delivery setup and actual provider acceptance are required. Requesting a receipt is separate from marketing consent.

features.title: Hosted receipt viewing
features.benefit: Give customers a readable receipt destination.
features.problem: A receipt email is more useful when its view link opens the recorded receipt.
features.workflow: Use the signed hosted-receipt link created for the supported receipt workflow.
features.example: A customer opens the receipt view from their transactional email.
features.fit: Access depends on a valid link and configured service. Keep receipt links private.

features.title: Receipt care notes
features.benefit: Keep available plant guidance close to the purchase.
features.problem: Customers may forget the care discussion once they get home.
features.workflow: Include eligible published care in the supported receipt rendering and delivery flow.
features.example: The shopper can revisit available light, watering and soil notes alongside the receipt.
features.fit: Only available reviewed guidance is included. This does not guarantee care coverage or enable a reminder campaign.

features.title: Separate marketing consent
features.benefit: Make the customer's choice clear.
features.problem: Asking for a receipt should not silently add someone to marketing.
features.workflow: Present the receipt request separately from the optional ongoing communications preference.
features.example: A customer requests a receipt and leaves the marketing option unchecked.
features.fit: Configure the store's actual consent wording and withdrawal process. A purchase is not marketing permission.

features.title: Bloom POS assistant
features.benefit: Ask a question and see where the answer came from.
features.problem: Owners need a practical way to find relevant store information.
features.workflow: Ask supported questions and review the cited records or guides before acting.
features.example: A manager asks where to begin with a recorded store issue and opens the cited workspace.
features.fit: Requires enabled AI configuration and authorized sources. It does not autonomously move money or make stock decisions.

features.title: Searchable POS guidebook
features.benefit: Find help in the language of the job.
features.problem: A staff member should not need an internal feature name to find instructions.
features.workflow: Search maintained guides or use supported cited how-to help.
features.example: A manager looks up the receiving routine before checking a delivery.
features.fit: Guides explain supported workflows. Store-specific policy and hardware still need training and review.

features.title: BloomSites product-photo sharing
features.benefit: Keep a matched product's photo consistent.
features.problem: Uploading the same photo separately for two products creates repetitive work.
features.workflow: Use the configured connection to share the approved photo for a matched product and review its status.
features.example: The manager checks whether a POS photo is waiting to share or confirmed on the website.
features.fit: Requires a configured BloomSites connection and verified product match. This is not universal catalogue or stock sync.

features.title: Reviewed migration
features.benefit: Switch with a plan for the records that matter.
features.problem: A hurried import can bring old mistakes into a new system.
features.workflow: Review the supported source adapter, dry run and control totals before applying approved records.
features.example: The owner checks product and balance totals with the migration team before a cutover.
features.fit: Adapters and available record types vary. Real exports and signed control totals need review; full historical migration is not assumed.

features.title: Hardware compatibility review
features.benefit: Keep equipment where it makes sense.
features.problem: Replacing a POS should start with understanding what the store already owns.
features.workflow: Review the iPad or browser device, scanner, printer, drawer and payment-reader requirements together.
features.example: The store identifies reusable equipment before ordering a new checkout bundle.
features.fit: Each model needs compatibility checks. Stripe readers require the correct account, region and integration; universal hardware support is not promised.

features.title: Offline cash selling
features.benefit: Keep eligible cash sales moving through an internet outage.
features.problem: An internet interruption should have a clear store procedure.
features.workflow: Use the prepared register's supported local cash workflow and review its visible synchronization status.
features.example: The connection drops during an eligible cash sale. Staff follow the prepared outage routine instead of guessing what is saved.
features.fit: Offline operation depends on a previously prepared device, store policy, current cached rules and required local backup setup. Offline card acceptance is not included.

features.title: Offline catalogue access
features.benefit: Keep downloaded product details within reach.
features.problem: A connection problem can make online-only product lists hard to use.
features.workflow: Use the prepared register's cached catalogue to find supported products and retained selling details.
features.example: Staff look up a downloaded plant record while the store internet is interrupted.
features.fit: Only previously downloaded records are available. Stock freshness, price rules, identity renewal and online-only payments have separate limits.

features.title: Saved work and sync status
features.benefit: See which saved work still needs attention.
features.problem: A completed local action is not the same as a confirmed server update.
features.workflow: Review pending and failed synchronization work and follow the retained recovery workflow.
features.example: After internet returns, the manager checks outstanding work rather than assuming every register is fully synchronized.
features.fit: Do not clear browser storage or replace a device with unsynchronized work. A visible queue is not proof of remote acknowledgement.

features.title: Offline backup and recovery
features.benefit: Plan for more than an internet outage.
features.problem: Saved data on one device can still be lost if that device fails.
features.workflow: Configure the supported store-network second-copy setup and verify acknowledgements before relying on it.
features.example: The owner rehearses a replacement-register recovery using the configured backup hub.
features.fit: Requires compatible local hardware, trusted connection setup and a physical recovery rehearsal. Unpaired stores cannot claim device-loss protection.

features.title: Plant and shelf labels
features.benefit: Make the label part of a better checkout.
features.problem: Accurate products still need clear labels that staff and customers can use.
features.workflow: Prepare supported label batches from catalogue, receiving or price-change work and review the layout.
features.example: A new delivery prompts a reviewed plant-label batch using the received product records.
features.fit: Zebra ZPL printing requires supported media and a configured private network bridge. A screen preview is not a successful physical barcode scan.

features.title: Network label printing from iPad
features.benefit: Bring label preparation closer to receiving.
features.problem: Tablet users need a workable route to compatible label printers.
features.workflow: Send supported label jobs through the configured network print bridge and review job status.
features.example: A manager prepares labels from a tablet after checking a delivery.
features.fit: iPad browser, network trust, printer, label media and actual scans require verification. Arbitrary Bluetooth printers are not automatically supported.

features.title: Plant guarantee claims
features.benefit: Handle a disappointing plant outcome with care.
features.problem: A guarantee conversation needs the original purchase and agreed terms.
features.workflow: Find the original receipt line, record the claim and review the evidence before approving an eligible remedy.
features.example: A customer brings back a failed shrub. The manager reviews the original terms and claim history before deciding.
features.fit: Eligibility requires owner review. Credit, replacement and provider refunds use their own verified workflows; dead stock never returns to sellable stock.

features.title: Loyalty rewards
features.benefit: Give a repeat visit a clear reward history.
features.problem: A reward programme needs balances that belong to real customers and purchases.
features.workflow: Use the reviewed policy and enrolled customer's verified sale history for supported earning, redemption and returns.
features.example: A regular shopper's eligible completed purchase contributes to the configured reward programme.
features.fit: Policy activation, enrollment, customer identity, currency and eligible payment combinations require setup. Unverified historical rewards are not spendable balances.

features.title: Margin and seasonal performance
features.benefit: Look beyond revenue when reviewing the season.
features.problem: A bigger sales total does not tell the whole profitability story.
features.workflow: Review seasonal performance alongside explicitly reviewed cost, inventory and labour evidence.
features.example: The owner compares a plant category's recorded sales with reviewed cost information before planning next season.
features.fit: Missing cost or labour evidence stays unavailable. Recorded purchase cost is not automatically a verified cost-of-goods-sold figure or profit guarantee.

features.title: Supplier shortages and backorders
features.benefit: Keep the missing part of a delivery visible.
features.problem: A short shipment should not make the remaining order disappear.
features.workflow: Review outstanding quantities, supplier shortages, backorders and supported remainder cancellation.
features.example: The grower cannot fill the last trays. Staff review the remainder without inventing stock for undelivered plants.
features.fit: Supplier commitments and substitute products need confirmation. Cancelling a remainder must preserve previous receipts and their costs.
